corrections: The historical statement that 5 Earth masses has a Schwarzschild radius of about 4.4 mm is off by a factor of 10; the correct radius is about 4.44 cm.
For 5e-5 solar masses the mass is about 16.65 Earth masses and the Schwarzschild radius is about 14.8 cm.
At about 583 AU, annual parallax has a semi-amplitude of about 5.90 arcmin, so any apparent sky position must be epoch- and observer-bound.
A 1-3 day cadence is too slow for the strongest point-lens photometric event if Earth-relative transverse motion dominates; characteristic t_E is minutes, not days.

bestiary.OWL: Separates three inconsistent historical mass conventions instead of blending them.
bestiary.HOUND: Repairs the factor-10 Schwarzschild-radius error and the 5e-5 Msun to Earth-mass mismatch.
bestiary.SPIDER: Converts distance plus mass hypotheses into a testable parallax/lensing observation graph.
bestiary.BELZEBUB: Rejects the old 1-3 day microlensing cadence as incapable of resolving minute-scale point-lens crossings if Earth motion dominates.

epistemic_boundary: Conditional prediction only; not evidence that the candidate exists or is a PBH.
